origin.description: Extract every run of code points that belong to a character class.
origin.usage: stri_extract_all_charclass(str, pattern, merge = TRUE, simplify = FALSE, omit_no_match = FALSE)

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: Character vector of strings to search.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.text: An ICU UnicodeSet pattern: \p{L}, \p{N}, \p{WhiteSpace}, [:WhiteSpace:], or [a-z]. A bare name such as WhiteSpace, and \w, are not patterns. An empty pattern is an error.

arguments.name: merge
arguments.text: If TRUE, join consecutive matching code points into one string.

arguments.name: simplify
arguments.text: If TRUE, return a character matrix padded with empty strings. NA pads with NA.

arguments.name: omit_no_match
arguments.text: If TRUE, a string with no match contributes an empty vector instead of NA.

origin.details: The default is a list of character vectors. A missing string or pattern is a one-element NA vector. simplify uses the first element when given a longer logical vector.
origin.value: A list of character vectors, or a character matrix when simplify is not FALSE.
origin.example:
x <- stri_extract_all_charclass("aab12", "\\p{L}")[[1]]
sentence <- paste0('stri_extract_all_charclass("aab12", "\\p{L}") returns ', paste(x, collapse = ", "), '.')
writeLines(sentence)

translation.description: Extract every run of code points that belong to a character class.

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: String, missing value, or list of those.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.text: An ICU UnicodeSet pattern: \p{L}, \p{N}, \p{WhiteSpace}, [:WhiteSpace:], or [a-z]. A bare name such as WhiteSpace, and \w, are not patterns. An empty pattern is an error. Membership is ICU 76, Unicode 16.

arguments.name: merge
arguments.text: If true, join consecutive matching code points into one string.

arguments.name: simplify
arguments.text: If true, return a list of rows padded with empty strings. NA pads with NA.

arguments.name: omit_no_match
arguments.text: If true, a string with no match contributes an empty list instead of NA.

translation.details: The default is a list of lists of strings. A missing string or pattern is a one-element NA list. simplify uses the first element when given a longer list.
translation.value: A list of lists of strings, or a list of rows when simplify is not false.
translation.example:
from stringi.charclass import stri_extract_all_charclass
x = stri_extract_all_charclass("aab12", "\\p{L}")
sentence = f'stri_extract_all_charclass("aab12", "\\p{{L}}") returns {", ".join(x[0])}.'
print(sentence)
